cards.explanation: The answer is pure lips, friends. The LORD says, "For then I will restore pure lips to the peoples, that all may call upon the name of the LORD and serve Him shoulder to shoulder." (Zephaniah 3:9) Notice the "all." He's not restoring this for a few folks in the front row. It's for the peoples.

The answer is True! The LORD says, "From beyond the rivers of Cush My worshipers, My scattered people, will bring Me an offering." (Zephaniah 3:10) Cush is a land south of Egypt, so that is a LONG way off. Even from way out there, His scattered people come bringing something to Him.

The answer is False, friends, and what a line this is. The LORD says, "On that day you will not be put to shame for any of the deeds by which you have transgressed against Me." (Zephaniah 3:11) Not for some of the deeds. ANY of them. I'd have been ready to sweat through the whole apron, and the text says no shame.

The word is pride, friends. The LORD says, "…I will remove from among you those who rejoice in their pride, and you will never again be haughty on My holy mountain." (Zephaniah 3:11) Haughty means looking down on everybody. The ones who rejoice in their pride are the ones He takes out of the batch.

The answer is a meek and humble people! The LORD says, "But I will leave within you a meek and humble people, and they will trust in the name of the LORD." (Zephaniah 3:12) The proud are removed, and the humble are the ones left standing. They are exactly who He keeps.
The word is trust, friends. "…they will trust in the name of the LORD." (Zephaniah 3:12) The meek and humble people lean on Him. They are not leaning on themselves.

The answer is feed and lie down, friends. The text says, "But they will feed and lie down, with no one to make them tremble." (Zephaniah 3:13) Eat, then rest. I'd call that a pretty good day, and nobody's making them shake.

The answer is their punishment, friends. "The LORD has taken away your punishment; He has turned back your enemy." (Zephaniah 3:15) That's the reason for all the shouting. When a weight like that is lifted, I'd be shouting too.

The answer is True! The call says, "Israel’s King, the LORD, is among you; no longer will you fear any harm." (Zephaniah 3:15) The King is right there among His people. That's the reason the fear can go.

The reason is that the LORD is among them and mighty to save, friends! "The LORD your God is among you; He is mighty to save." (Zephaniah 3:17) The reason not to fear isn't a wall or an army. It's WHO is with them. And He is right in the middle of them.

The word is quiet, friends. "He will quiet you with His love…" (Zephaniah 3:17) After all that talk of fear in this passage, I think that sounds like a gift. The same verse says, "He will rejoice over you with singing." Rejoicing, gladness and singing are all in that one verse.

The ones He gathers are those who grieve over the appointed feasts, friends. The LORD says, "I will gather those among you who grieve over the appointed feasts, so that you will no longer suffer reproach." (Zephaniah 3:18) The ones who are hurting get gathered. And the reproach stops.

The word is lame, friends. The LORD says, "I will save the lame and gather the scattered…" (Zephaniah 3:19) He names the lame right there in the promise, next to the scattered. He says plainly that He will save them.

The answer is False, friends, and what a turnaround. The LORD says, "…I will appoint praise and fame for the disgraced throughout the earth." (Zephaniah 3:19) The disgraced are not hidden away. They get praise and fame, all across the earth.

The answer is their captives, friends. The LORD says, "…I will give you fame and praise among all the peoples of the earth when I restore your captives before your very eyes…" (Zephaniah 3:20) Before their very eyes! They get to watch it happen.
